collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A storyteller wants to tell the founders' jokes and mistakes too: tell the whole of them, or keep to the honored stories.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is the village storyteller, and (subject.he/she) has decided the children should know the founders as real people: the one who was afraid of crabs, the one who sang terribly, the one who got lost going to the toilet. (friend) thinks that is disrespectful. What should (subject) tell?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells the funny stories and the brave ones together. The children love the founders more than ever. (friend) laughs despite (friend.him/her)self at the crab story. Some elders are scandalized. Some are delighted.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tells only the great deeds. The children are impressed and a little bored. Later, (subject) tells (friend) the crab story privately. (friend) laughs so hard (friend.he/she) has to sit down, and asks for more.
